takeaway: H. pylori is a Gram-negative spiral microaerophilic rod that makes urease, causes peptic ulcers, is diagnosed on biopsy and can be spread iatrogenically; Gram-positive is the exception.

question.text: A 28-year-old man with gastritis is H. pylori positive. All of the following about H. pylori are true except:

answer.text: It is Gram-positive. H. pylori is actually Gram-negative.
answer.say: It is Gram-positive. H. pylori is actually Gram-negative.

lines.text: Helicobacter pylori is a spiral, motile, microaerophilic organism living in the stomach.
It makes urease, which breaks urea into ammonia and raises the surrounding pH.
Infection raises gastric acid and can lead to peptic ulceration.
It can be diagnosed with a biopsy at endoscopy, and the scope can even spread it iatrogenically.
But it is Gram-negative, not Gram-positive.
